rows.description: A quiet, satisfied chortle can mean genuine amusement, smug pleasure or relief. Context decides: shared humour bonds people, but the same sound aimed at someone's mistake can feel mocking.

rows.subtype: Types of laughter and social bonding [Expressing]
rows.description: A young adult uses chuckles, belly laughs and guffaws to show amusement and connection. Shared, spontaneous laughter builds closeness, while a cackle or guffaw may feel bold in one culture and normal in another.

rows.description: A young adult cries after exams, a breakup or a hard job. Tears can release tension and are not weakness; rest, talking to a friend and seeking counselling if crying is frequent or with hopeless thoughts are wise steps.

rows.description: A young adult weeps at a funeral, a farewell, a wedding or a graduation. Tears can mean grief, joy or relief, and cultures differ in how openly they are shown, so support respects the person's own meaning.

rows.description: A young adult joins cheering and whooping at a concert, match or graduation. Volume and style are welcome in some settings and odd in others, so awareness of the venue and other people is a form of respect.

rows.subtype: Yelling at work or home and de-escalation [Regulating]
rows.description: A young adult notices a raised voice from a colleague or partner and stays calm, lowers their own tone and asks to continue later. Shouting that frightens or controls another person is not acceptable, and leaving and getting support is right.

rows.subtype: Sighing to hide or show stress [Regulating]
rows.description: A young adult takes a slow sigh to calm down or lets out an audible sigh in frustration. Deliberate slow breathing can steady nerves, while a loud sigh at a colleague may feel dismissive, so awareness of audience matters.

rows.description: A young adult whistles or hums for calm or joy, but whistling at a person in public can be unwelcome harassment. Recognising when a sound crosses into disrespect helps, and anyone targeted may leave and report it.
